_readme: XSSentinel LLM provider pool -- used ONLY to write the narrative report
(--ai-report).  It never decides whether something is vulnerable: findings,
severity, URLs and PoCs always come from the deterministic engine.
Failover order = the order below.  Within a provider the expansion is
model-outer / key-inner, because a provider's several keys are quota
redundancy for the same model list: the preferred model is tried across
every key before a lesser model is used.
Ordering evidence: every candidate was measured generating a REAL report
(~800-1500 output tokens), not a 16-token ping -- the two rankings differ a
lot.  ping latency ranks AMD DeepSeek-V4-Flash first (0.9s) while it times
out past 150s on real output; that is why it sits late here.
Per-candidate state (cooldown after a 429 / 401 / timeout / empty body /
truncated body) is persisted next to this file in llm_state.json, so a
rate-limit window survives across processes.  Clear every cooldown with
`python -m xssentinel --ai-reset`, or just delete that file.
Keys can be overridden without editing this file:
XSSENTINEL_LLM_KEY_AMD=..., XSSENTINEL_LLM_KEY_SENSENOVA=... (comma-separated)
A different pool: XSSENTINEL_LLM_CONFIG=/path/to/pool.json
Health-check every candidate at any time with:
python -m xssentinel --ai-check

providers.label: SenseNova (token.sensenova.cn)
providers.note: First choice: 3 independent keys, and the only pool whose real-output latency was measured as good. deepseek-v4-flash produced a complete ~1700-char report in 9.3s (930 output tokens) and is therefore ranked first across all 3 keys. kimi-k3 answered a ping in 6.1s (real-output latency untested). glm-5.2 is kept third: it answered a ping in 0.8s but burned its entire 1500-token budget on its reasoning channel and returned only 95 characters of answer -- the pool now rejects a completion below report_ai.MIN_REPORT_CHARS as truncated_response, so that costs one failover rather than a stub report. deepseek-v4-flash intermittently returns an empty 200 body; empty_response handles it. deepseek-v4.1-flash is 403 'model is not available in the current token plan' and is not listed.

providers.label: AMD Radeon Cloud (developer.amd.com.cn)
providers.note: Second choice: smallest, fastest model first because AMD's latency is the least predictable of the three pools. Measured 2026-09-22 on REAL report output: DeepSeek-V4-Flash timed out past 150s (and past 45s in an end-to-end run) even though a 16-token ping answered in 0.9s -- it is kept second only because its output quality is the best here when it does answer. MiniCPM5-2B is the steady one (0.5s ping, and it wrote a complete 1517-char report in an end-to-end run); note it leaks its reasoning channel ahead of the answer, which report_ai.clean_completion strips. GLM-5.3-Flash and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash answered 429 'at its concurrency limit (8 / 32)': reachable but heavily shared, so they sit last. Qwen3.8-* answered 200 with an EMPTY body and is deliberately omitted.

providers.label: NVIDIA NIM (integrate.api.nvidia.com)
providers.note: Last resort: slow but real capacity when the others are cooling or rate-limited. Probed 2026-09-22: deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4.1-flash answered a ping in 23.8s; z-ai/glm-5.3-flash timed out twice at 45s (cold start) -- raise --ai-timeout if this pool matters. The model the original note named, z-ai/glm-5.2, is GONE (HTTP 410, end of life 2026-08-21) and has been replaced by the vendor's own successor glm-5.3-flash.

providers.label: OpenRouter (openrouter.ai)
providers.note: DISABLED -- the account cannot infer. Probed 2026-09-22: every model returns 403 'Inference is blocked on this account. Please contact support@openrouter.ai', and the paid path returns 402 'Insufficient credits. This account never purchased credits'. The model named in the note, stealth/ox-alpha, no longer exists (404: 'Thank you for participating in the Stealth Ox Alpha testing period. This model was ZAI's GLM-5.3 Flash. Use it now: z-ai/glm-5.3-flash'). Flip enabled to true only after the account is fixed.
